title: Modular Arithmetic, Divisibility, Primes & Euler Totient

sections.heading: Modular Arithmetic, Divisibility, Primes & Euler Totient Practice Exercises

questions.q: Using Legendre's prime-valuation theorem, how many trailing zeros appear at the end of \( 35! \) in base \( 10 \)?
questions.answer: Since \( 10 = 2 \cdot 5 \) and \( v_2(35!) > v_5(35!) \), the number of trailing zeros equals \( v_5(35!) = \lfloor 35/5 \rfloor + \lfloor 35/25 \rfloor + \lfloor 35/125 \rfloor = 7 + 1 + 0 = 8 \).

questions.q: Let \( x \) be the smallest positive integer satisfying the simultaneous congruences \( x \equiv 3 \pmod{5} \) (whose initial progression is marked on the number line) and \( x \equiv 6 \pmod{7} \). Find \( x \).
questions.answer: Write \( x = 5k + 3 \) and substitute into the second congruence: \( 5k + 3 \equiv 6 \pmod{7} \). Solving modulo \( 7 \) gives the unique residue modulo \( 5 \cdot 7 = 35 \), yielding smallest positive solution \( x = 13 \) (check: \( 13 = 2\cdot 5 + 3 \) and \( 13 = 1\cdot 7 + 6 \)).

questions.q: Let \( x \) be the smallest positive integer satisfying the simultaneous congruences \( x \equiv 1 \pmod{5} \) (whose initial progression is marked on the number line) and \( x \equiv 7 \pmod{9} \). Find \( x \).
questions.answer: Write \( x = 5k + 1 \) and substitute into the second congruence: \( 5k + 1 \equiv 7 \pmod{9} \). Solving modulo \( 9 \) gives the unique residue modulo \( 5 \cdot 9 = 45 \), yielding smallest positive solution \( x = 16 \) (check: \( 16 = 3\cdot 5 + 1 \) and \( 16 = 1\cdot 9 + 7 \)).

questions.q: Let \( x \) be the smallest positive integer satisfying the simultaneous congruences \( x \equiv 5 \pmod{7} \) (whose initial progression is marked on the number line) and \( x \equiv 1 \pmod{9} \). Find \( x \).
questions.answer: Write \( x = 7k + 5 \) and substitute into the second congruence: \( 7k + 5 \equiv 1 \pmod{9} \). Solving modulo \( 9 \) gives the unique residue modulo \( 7 \cdot 9 = 63 \), yielding smallest positive solution \( x = 19 \) (check: \( 19 = 2\cdot 7 + 5 \) and \( 19 = 2\cdot 9 + 1 \)).

questions.q: Let \( x \) be the smallest positive integer satisfying the simultaneous congruences \( x \equiv 1 \pmod{7} \) (whose initial progression is marked on the number line) and \( x \equiv 0 \pmod{11} \). Find \( x \).
questions.answer: Write \( x = 7k + 1 \) and substitute into the second congruence: \( 7k + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{11} \). Solving modulo \( 11 \) gives the unique residue modulo \( 7 \cdot 11 = 77 \), yielding smallest positive solution \( x = 22 \) (check: \( 22 = 3\cdot 7 + 1 \) and \( 22 = 2\cdot 11 + 0 \)).

questions.q: Given that \( p = 11 \) is prime, find the least non-negative remainder when \( 9! \) is divided by \( 11 \).
questions.answer: By Wilson's Theorem, \( 10! \equiv -1 \pmod{11} \). Factoring out the top \( 1 \) terms gives \( 10! = (10) \cdot 9! \equiv (-1)^{1} 1! \cdot 9! \equiv -1 \pmod{11} \). Inverting modulo \( 11 \) yields \( 9! \equiv 1 \pmod{11} \).

questions.q: Given that \( p = 13 \) is prime, find the least non-negative remainder when \( 10! \) is divided by \( 13 \).
questions.answer: By Wilson's Theorem, \( 12! \equiv -1 \pmod{13} \). Factoring out the top \( 2 \) terms gives \( 12! = (12)(11) \cdot 10! \equiv (-1)^{2} 2! \cdot 10! \equiv -1 \pmod{13} \). Inverting modulo \( 13 \) yields \( 10! \equiv 6 \pmod{13} \).

questions.q: Given that \( p = 17 \) is prime, find the least non-negative remainder when \( 13! \) is divided by \( 17 \).
questions.answer: By Wilson's Theorem, \( 16! \equiv -1 \pmod{17} \). Factoring out the top \( 3 \) terms gives \( 16! = (16)(15)(14) \cdot 13! \equiv (-1)^{3} 3! \cdot 13! \equiv -1 \pmod{17} \). Inverting modulo \( 17 \) yields \( 13! \equiv 3 \pmod{17} \).

questions.q: Given that \( p = 19 \) is prime, find the least non-negative remainder when \( 17! \) is divided by \( 19 \).
questions.answer: By Wilson's Theorem, \( 18! \equiv -1 \pmod{19} \). Factoring out the top \( 1 \) terms gives \( 18! = (18) \cdot 17! \equiv (-1)^{1} 1! \cdot 17! \equiv -1 \pmod{19} \). Inverting modulo \( 19 \) yields \( 17! \equiv 1 \pmod{19} \).

questions.q: How many integers \( k \in \{1, 2, \dots, 36\} \) are relatively prime to \( 36 \) (i.e., find Euler's totient \( \varphi(36) \))?
questions.answer: Using Euler's product formula \( \varphi(n) = n \prod_{p \mid n}\left(1 - \frac{1}{p}\right) \) on the prime factorization of \( 36 \), we obtain \( \varphi(36) = 12 \).
